land.text: Sophene, the Orontid lands round Arsamosata

predecessors.note: The Orontids ruled Armenia as satraps and kings (c. 404-330 and after); Sophene 'emerged as a distinct kingdom' in the mid-3rd century. Cliopatria's Armenia row is flagged as probably two states.

land.text: Sophene, conquered by Tigranes c. 95 with Acilisene, Zariadres's conquest drawn as Sophene's to 95

successors.note: Cliopatria's Armenia shapes hold these cells only from -80 (not -90..-81): the Armenia dossier should gain Sophene at -95. fx-46 review: Acilisene (ledger 2, keyframes -188 and -110) added to the land, so that its cells pass to Armenia with the rest of the kingdom in 95 ('Sophene was conquered by the King of Greater Armenia, Tigranes II the Great') instead of falling to nobody.

capitals.name: Arsamosata (Elazig area)
capitals.note: 'Arsamosata was the largest settlement and the only true city'; the ruins lie in Elazig province, the gazetteer's Elazig point is used as an approximation.

capitals.name: Carcathiocerta (Egil)
capitals.note: 'a second royal capital, probably founded by Arkathias in the later 2nd century BCE', identified with modern Egil on the Tigris; the Zariadres page has the royal city renamed Epiphaneia under Zariadres. Coordinates and the start year are approximate.

keyframe_review.note: 17.1 k km2 on the upper Euphrates and Tigris round Arsamosata (lon 38.8-40.7, lat 38.2-39.6). 'Established: 3rd century BCE'; Scholars think it 'emerged as a distinct kingdom in the mid-3rd century BCE, when Seleucid influence was declining'. The page gives no area, so no area check.
17.0 k km2, unchanged; the page names Sames I (c. 260) and Arsames I (c. 240) as Orontid kings and records no border change.
17.0 k km2, unchanged; nothing on the page for these two years.

17.0 k km2, unchanged. Dependent on the Seleucids from c. 212 ('Antiochus III attacked Sophene ... Xerxes submitted and married Antiochus's sister, Antiochis') and, c. 190, under his general Zariadres; the vassal tint belongs to the Seleucid dossier.

17.0 k km2 for -188..-111. After Apamea 'Zariadres ruled Sophene and Artaxias ruled Greater Armenia' (188, with Roman consent) and Zariadres took Acilisene, Derxene (possibly) and Karenitis (possibly); the Kingdom page adds Akisene (possibly Anzitene). None of these is dated and Cliopatria's shape does not change, so the shape stands and the districts are ledger events at confidence 1. fx-46 (request R004): Acilisene added so that the ledger gain of -188 (ledger/2) is not undone by the keyframe snap of this shape's first year; the Kingdom of Sophene page: 'Zariadres conquered Acilisene to the north' (map caption: territories conquered during the reign of Zariadres, c. 190-163 BC). The conquest has no year of its own, -188 is the dossier's bridging reading.

region.text: Sophene round Arsamosata, split from Orontid Armenia

ledger.note: 256: Sophene becomes a kingdom. The page says Sophene 'emerged as a distinct kingdom in the mid-3rd century BCE, when Seleucid influence was declining' (infobox 'Established: 3rd century BCE'); the Orontids ruled Armenia as satraps and kings before. The year is Cliopatria's.

190: Zariadres takes the royal title. 'After Antiochus was defeated by the Romans, Zariadres took the royal title and became independent. Artaxias did the same in Greater Armenia.' He had been installed by Antiochus III (c. 190 on this page, c. 200 on the Zariadres page) after the Orontid Xerxes was poisoned (c. 212). Dynastic change, same state; the Zariadres page confirms the rebellion of 190 and Roman consent in 188.

region.text: Acilisene, the upper Euphrates round Erzincan

ledger.note: After 188: Zariadres expands. 'Zariadres and Artaxias then allied and expanded their territories. Zariadres took Acilisene and Akisene (possibly Anzitene), plus unnamed lands to the east'; the Zariadres page adds Karenitis and Derxene (possible) and Taronitis (Zariadres or Artaxias). None is dated, so the year is a bridging reading at the treaty. Fixed in fx-46 (request R004): the gazetteer has no 'Akisene', and the Kingdom of Sophene page calls it 'the otherwise unknown Akisene to the west', 'possibly a corruption of Anzitene/Handzit', without a location, so it is dropped and the event holds Acilisene alone, which the page and the Zariadres page ('Zariadres conquered [Acilisene]') both give to Zariadres (reign c. 190-163 BC, no year for the conquest).

region.text: the kingdom of Sophene: the upper Euphrates and Tigris round Arsamosata, with Acilisene (ledger 2)

ledger.note: c. 95: Tigranes the Great conquers Sophene. Infobox 'Conquered: c. 95 BCE, by Tigranes the Great of Greater Armenia'; he 'deposed Artanes', the last king (the Tigranes page: accession 96/95, no date for Sophene).

wars.name: Antiochus III's campaign against Xerxes of Sophene
wars.outcome: Xerxes submitted and married Antiochus's sister Antiochis; later sources say she poisoned him on Antiochus's orders.
wars.note: c. 212 BCE; the Zariadres page also allows 202/201.

wars.name: Rebellion of Zariadres and Artaxias against the Seleucids
wars.outcome: After Magnesia Zariadres took the royal title; under the Treaty of Apamea (188) Antiochus III gave up the lands north and west of the Taurus, 'which included Sophene and Greater Armenia'.

wars.name: Tigranes the Great's conquest of Sophene
wars.outcome: Tigranes deposed Artanes, the last king, c. 95; Parthia had forced Sophene to accept its suzerainty under Mithridates II (124-91).

certainty.note: The page describes Sophene by its neighbours (Acilisene to the north, Akisene to the west, the Taurus to the south under Apamea) and gives no treaty line; every frontier is soft.

sources.title: Kingdom of Sophene
sources.note: Identity, mid-3rd-century origin, Xerxes 212, Zariadres 190/188, Parthian suzerainty, Tigranes c. 95, Pompey, Sohaemus c. 54 CE.

sources.title: Zariadres
sources.note: Seleucid strategos, 190 rebellion, 188 recognition, districts taken (Acilisene, Derxene, Karenitis, Taronitis).

sources.title: Tigranes the Great

sources.title: Sohaemus of Armenia

notes: Pages: five opened (budget 5; Zariadris failed, Zariadres loaded). Cliopatria rows: the Roman-era shapes (-63, 23, 43, 106: 23.8 k km2 each, -63..113) are marked wrong because the Kingdom of Sophene page ends the kingdom c. 95 BCE and has no independent Sophene afterwards; only c. 54 CE does it have 'Rome installed Sohaemus of Emesa as king of Sophene'. The pages opened do not settle who held the land in 66 BCE-113 CE ('debated whether Sophene returned to Greater Armenia or became part of Cappadocia'), and the two pages meant to date the Roman period (Sohaemus of Armenia, Ariobarzanes I) are thin; a gap-filler should open 'Gordyene', 'Sophene (province)' and 'Corbulo' pages, and 'Roman-Parthian War of 58-63'. The shape -110..-88 ends 8 years after the page's c. 95; Cliopatria's Armenia holds the cells from -80, so -94..-81 is a hole the Armenia dossier should close. Vassal relations are the overlord's record: the Seleucid dossier needs vassal_start kingdom-of-sophene c. 212 to c. 190, the Parthian dossier vassal_start/vassal_end kingdom-of-sophene (under Mithridates II, 124-91, to c. 95). Disagreements: Zariadres installed c. 190 (Sophene page, Strabo) or c. 200 (Zariadres page, Lang); Xerxes' death c. 212 or 202/201; Carcathiocerta founded by Arkathias in the later 2nd century (Sophene page) or renamed Epiphaneia by Zariadres (Zariadres page). Gazetteer names needed: Acilisene (Erzincan plain) and Akisene (possibly Anzitene, round Kigi/Palu) are real districts the gazetteer lacks; the events using them have no cells until it adds them. Arsamosata and Eğil coordinates are approximations. The Kingdom of Sophene page gives no area figure, so the 17 k km2 core could not be checked.
